from: Measurement team, with the account team
bottom_line: Short-form video pays back in sales: about KRW 1.2 of extra sales per won during the test (range 0.6-1.8), and about 1.5 counting the two weeks after it, when part of the effect lands. The 4-week summer pause cost about KRW 94M in sales (range KRW 30M-KRW 161M), not the KRW 245M a before/after view suggests.

The jump in reported search revenue after switching to AI auto-bidding (+93%) is almost entirely sales that were already happening, now credited to search. Total sales did not move (-0.2%, range -2.0% to +1.6%).
The 30% search budget increase that followed returned about KRW 0.15 per won (range -0.35 to 0.64): below break-even.

Added up, the platforms claim 1.3 times the sales that ads actually added. Short video is the only channel credited with less than it adds. At today's spend, the next won returns less than a won in every channel (model: 0.3-0.8), so shift budget first and then test a smaller total.

In profit terms (gross margin assumed at 40%), short video pays back if a new customer's lifetime purchases reach 1.6x their first; the next won in any channel needs at least 3.2x. Your repeat-purchase data decides whether to add budget.

measured.question: Does short video add sales?
measured.method: Geo test, 20 matched region pairs, 6 weeks
measured.answer: Yes. iROAS 1.20 (0.58-1.81); 1.52 with a 2-week cooldown; brand searches -5.3% in regions without video
measured.confidence: High: A/A-checked design, one contaminated pair found and removed

measured.question: What did the summer pause cost?
measured.confidence: Medium: wide range, but consistent with the geo test

measured.question: Is auto-bidding adding sales?
measured.method: Total sales around the switch + 456 placebo dates
measured.confidence: High for 'no large effect'; a gain under ~2% cannot be ruled out

measured.question: How to split next year's budget?
measured.method: Media mix model checked against both experiments
measured.answer: Move money from retargeting and search to short video; keep the total flat
measured.confidence: Medium: search is the least certain channel

recommendation.note: Moves are capped where the model is unsure (risk-aware plan). Revisit search after the next test.

profit.note: Returns are in sales, from the 104-week model. A won of ad spend pays back when return x gross margin x lifetime multiple is at least 1. 'Lifetime multiple' = a new customer's total purchases divided by their first, which only PAWLY's own order data can tell. Margin of 40% is a placeholder.

rows.item: Cost of the geo test (sales lost incl. cooldown, minus video budget withheld)
rows.basis: 77.5M sales lost vs 50.8M not spent, 19 pairs

rows.item: Sales a repeat of the 4-week video pause would cost
rows.basis: Causal impact read of the summer pause; the geo test shows the loss is real

rows.item: Yearly loss if the 30% search increase had been kept
rows.basis: 23.7M extra spend returned 3.4M sales per 4 weeks, x13

rows.item: Expected yearly gain from the reallocation

worth_it.note: The geo test cost about KRW 27M in sales. Each decision it and the follow-up reads support is worth several times that a year. In sales terms; profit depends on margin and repeat buying.

not_sure: Search's return is the widest range in the model (90%: 0.4-1.7). A plan built on the model's average alone would cut search 27%; this plan trims it 12% and leaves any bigger cut to the search test.
The pause estimate rests on a model, not a holdout; treat it as supporting the geo test, not replacing it.
Profit depends on repeat buying we have not measured yet; until then, read every return as sales, not profit.

next_test.what: Search holdout: switch search off in 30% of regions (chosen within size bands) for 6 weeks, plus a 2-week cooldown
next_test.why: Search is where uncertainty costs the most; a direct test settles the next budget decision
next_test.eligibility: A 30% holdout detects a return of 0.75 or more, almost as sensitive as switching off half the regions (0.7), with about 59% of the sales at risk

learning_agenda.question: What does search really add?
learning_agenda.study: Search holdout in 30% of regions, 6 weeks + 2-week cooldown
learning_agenda.why_now: Widest model range of any channel (90%: 0.4-1.7); reported ROAS 3.4

learning_agenda.question: Is the total budget too high?
learning_agenda.study: Step-down test: matched regions run all channels 20% lower for 6 weeks
learning_agenda.why_now: Marginal ROI below 1 in every channel (model 0.3-0.8)

learning_agenda.question: How much of retargeting is re-credited?
learning_agenda.study: Audience holdout: 15% of retargeting audiences not served for 4 weeks

learning_agenda.question: What is next year's plan?
learning_agenda.study: Refit the media mix model with every experiment so far as calibration; brand lift survey during a video flight
learning_agenda.decides: 2028 budget split and the upper-funnel KPI
learning_agenda.why_now: Each experiment narrows one channel's range; the survey adds the brand side the sales tests miss

asks: Share the media plan before each test: booked budgets are the denominator of every return figure.
Share gross margin and repeat-purchase rates by first-purchase month, so returns can be read as profit.
Tell us about regional promotions during a test (the G26 retail promotion would have inflated the result by about a quarter).
Keep budgets flat during tests, and send daily total sales from your own order system.
account_team_notes: Growth opportunity: short video +15% is about KRW 192M more video spend a year, backed by an experiment, not by the platform's own report.
Position search as 'prove, then reinvest', not as a cut: the holdout either confirms its value or frees budget for video.
The total-budget step-down builds trust: an advertiser who sees us test spending less believes us when we ask for more.
Studies to propose next: 30% regional holdout for search, audience holdout for retargeting, brand lift survey for video, recalibrated MMM.
Reusable for the next client: the study-selection table and the eligibility calculation (power from past weeks, A/A calibration) run on any region-by-day sales table in the same format.
